subject: Post-call: logging & redaction approach for MediQ pilot
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
To: Ananya Rao <ananya@mediq-health.com>, Raj Patel <raj.patel@mediq-health.com>
Cc: security@mediq-health.com
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap: logging controls and redaction options (next steps)

Thanks again for taking the time today — good conversation. Capturing the outcomes and proposed next steps so we have a single place to track: 

Summary of your priorities (as we heard them)
- Avoid storing customer PII in plaintext in any long-term logs (PII = SSNs, full credit cards, PHI identifiers).
- Be able to sanitize request/response bodies and strip or pseudonymize trace IDs/headers before logs are persisted and exported to downstream systems.
- Maintain short-term fidelity for debugging (you want higher-resolution logs for 7–14 days, then scrubbed versions afterwards).
- Data residency: logs for EU patients must remain in eu region; US logs in us region.

Proposed immediate actions from Redwood
1) Share a short redaction approach doc (attached: redaction-proposal-v1.pdf) that maps runtime masking vs post-process scrubbing.
2) Provide a sample redaction config you can run in our sandbox (attached: sample-redaction-config.json).
3) Confirm what we can surface in the pilot: encrypted 90-day raw retention for debugging (access-controlled), 30-day scrubbed retention for long-term analytics, and automatic trace ID pseudonymization for exports.
4) Schedule a technical design call with your engineering/security team next week to walk the data-flow diagram (attached: data-flow-diagram.png).

Questions for you
- Can you confirm whether your compliance team requires SOC 2 type II evidence before a sandbox pilot or only for production?
- Any specific headers you always need preserved (besides standard request-id/trace-id)?

Next proposed timeline
- Send design doc + sample config today (ACTION: me)
- Technical call: Tue/Wed next week (ACTION: Ananya/Raj to confirm availability)
- Pilot start: target 12/14 (dependent on SOC / POA)

Thanks — I cc'ed our security alias for visibility.

— Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
stephanie@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0182

From: Ananya Rao <ananya@mediq-health.com>

Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 09:24:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: logging controls and redaction options (next steps)

Thanks Stephanie — appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side before we lock the call: 

1) Residency: For PHI-containing logs we need them to remain physically in the EU region for EU patients. We will share the patient-region mapping logic on Monday. Does Redwood offer region-bound log buckets for the pilot?

2) Trace IDs / headers: We need to preserve request->response mapping for debugging but do NOT want raw trace IDs in logs sent to our analytics pipeline. Can you confirm if you support deterministic pseudonymization (same trace ID maps to same pseudonym) so we can correlate events without seeing originals?

3) Retention windows: Your 90-day encrypted raw + 30-day scrubbed model sounds promising. For production we may want 14-day raw + archive-only scrubbed at 365 days. Can the retention windows be configured per-account or per-route?

4) Compliance evidence: our legal team expects SOC 2 attestation for prod but for pilots we can accept SOC 2 in-progress and evidence of controls (logs access controls, KMS integration). Please attach any SOC / security whitepaper you can share.

We can do Tue 12/1 10–11 PST for the technical call. Will you send a calendar invite?

Thanks,
Ananya
Head of Platform Security | MediQ Health
ananya@mediq-health.com
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 08:07:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Post-call recap: logging controls and redaction options (next steps)

Fwd-ing Ananya's response — they confirmed Tue 12/1 10–11 PST. Two asks:

Rishi — can you prepare a one-pager that outlines the two implementation patterns we discussed: 
- Runtime masking (agent/runtime-level): mask PII at request ingress; pros: never writes PII to disk; cons: higher tail latency for some routes.
- Post-process scrubbing: write encrypted raw for short window (configurable), then run scrubber to redact stored logs before exports; pros: minimal runtime impact; cons: requires short-term access to raw data (access-controlled).
Include: recommended default retention (we think 14d raw / 30d scrubbed for pilots), deterministic pseudonymization approach for trace IDs (HMAC with per-customer salt + truncated digest), and notes about retaining hashed trace IDs for analytics. Also include how we can region-isolate log buckets for EU vs US. Attach sample-redaction-config.json (already in attachments).

Ben — please draft a pilot commercial that covers 4-week sandbox access + optional dedicated 1-week extended debugging window (priced separately). We need an estimate for engineering effort to enable region-bound buckets and the scrubber pipeline for the pilot.

I'll draft the calendar invite and attach the design doc.

— Stephanie
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Post-call recap: logging controls and redaction options (next steps)

Thanks — quick technical reply to seed the one-pager: 

A) Trace ID pseudonymization- Approach: HMAC-SHA256(trace_id, customer_salt) -> base64url -> keep first 16 chars. Deterministic; same input -> same pseudonym. Store salt in KMS and limit decryption to ops for post-mortem. This preserves correlation without exposing originals.

B) Runtime masking vs post-process (pros/cons)- Runtime masking: use streaming parser hooks in the request pipeline to redact fields defined in the redaction-config. Lower storage risk, immediate; requires per-route config and small CPU cost.
- Post-process scrubbing: ingest encrypted raw logs to a customer-region S3/GCS bucket, run scrubber job (k8s batch) to apply rules and write scrubbed output to analytics buckets. Keep raw encrypted for N days (configurable).

C) Retention defaults for pilot
- Recommended pilot config: 14d encrypted raw (debug), 30d scrubbed logs (analytics)
- Production options: configurable per-route/account: 7/30/90/365 windows supported with policy engine.

D) Region isolation
- We can pin ingestion and storage to region-specific clusters. For EU patient data we map ingestion to eu-1, write logs to eu-only storage, and enforce KMS keys scoped to eu region.

E) Access controls & evidence
- We will attach the security whitepaper and SOC status to the calendar invite. For pilot we can provide scoped audit logs showing who accessed raw logs.

I attached a minimal sample-redaction-config.json for their team to review (same file in thread attachments). For the call I can walk through the HMAC pseudonymization and show quick perf numbers (masking adds ~2–6% p95 on a 1kB payload for our microbench).

If Ben needs an engineering estimate I can sketch the work items: region bucket wiring (2 dev days), scrubber pipeline config + testing (3–4 dev days), UI toggles for retention (2 dev days). Total ~1–1.5 sprint work to get pilot-ready.

— Rishi
